title: Rigveda 1.60: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.60: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.60 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 42r-42v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.60.1-5 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 4, varga 26); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 42v
translation.original_text:
1vahni̍ṁ ya̱śasa̍ṁ vi̱datha̍sya ke̱tuṁ su̍prā̱vya̍ṁ dū̱taṁ sa̱dyoa̍rtham | dvi̱janmā̍naṁ ra̱yim i̍va praśa̱staṁ rā̱tim bha̍ra̱d bhṛga̍ve māta̱riśvā̍ ||
2a̱sya śāsu̍r u̱bhayā̍saḥ sacante ha̱viṣma̍nta u̱śijo̱ ye ca̱ martā̍ḥ | di̱vaś ci̱t pūrvo̱ ny a̍sādi̱ hotā̱pṛcchyo̍ vi̱śpati̍r vi̱kṣu ve̱dhāḥ ||
3taṁ navya̍sī hṛ̱da ā jāya̍mānam a̱smat su̍kī̱rtir madhu̍jihvam aśyāḥ | yam ṛ̱tvijo̍ vṛ̱jane̱ mānu̍ṣāsa̱ḥ praya̍svanta ā̱yavo̱ jīja̍nanta ||
4u̱śik pā̍va̱ko vasu̱r mānu̍ṣeṣu̱ vare̍ṇyo̱ hotā̍dhāyi vi̱kṣu | damū̍nā gṛ̱hapa̍ti̱r dama̱ ām̐ a̱gnir bhu̍vad rayi̱patī̍ rayī̱ṇām ||
5taṁ tvā̍ va̱yam pati̍m agne rayī̱ṇām pra śa̍ṁsāmo ma̱tibhi̱r gota̍māsaḥ | ā̱śuṁ na vā̍jambha̱ram ma̱rjaya̍ntaḥ prā̱tar ma̱kṣū dhi̱yāva̍sur jagamyāt ||
translation.text:
1As 'twere Some goodly treasure Mâtariṣvan brought, as a gift, the glorious Priest to Bhr̥igu, Banner of sacrifice, the good Protector, child of two births, the swiftly moving envoy.
2Both Gods and men obey this Ruler's order, Gods who are worshipped, men who yearn and worship. As Priest he takes his seat ere break of morning, House-Lord, adorable with men, Ordainer.
3May our fair praise, heart-born, most recent, reach him whose tongue, e'en at his birth, is sweet as honey; Whom mortal priests, men, with their strong endeavour, supplied with dainty viands, have created.
4Good to mankind, the yearning Purifier hath among men been placed as Priest choice-worthy. May Agni be our Friend, Lord of the Household, protector of the riches in the dwelling.
5As such we Gotamas with hymns extol thee, O Agni, as the guardian Lord of riches, Decking thee like a horse, the swift prizewinner. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 42v (OPenn image 44, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.60.1 ‹supra-avyam dūtam sadyaḥ-artham dvi-janmānam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 43r, begins in RV 1.61.2 ‹indrāya hṛdā manasā manīṣā›. Verses 1.60.1-5 end on this page; 1.60.1 begins on fol. 42r.
